# TiffCraft

TiffCraft is a header-only C++20 library for reading uncompressed TIFF images.
It provides a customizable image-data export interface and requires no separate
library binary.

# Objectives

TiffCraft is designed based on the following principles:

- Permissive license: to be used in open source and proprietary software.
- C++ header-only: to easy integration onto existing projects.
- Flexible but simple API: for ease of use.
- Feature complete: to cover a wide variety of use cases.
  - TiffCraft is NOT feature complete at this time! The objective is for guiding
    on-going development.

# Usage

For quick access to TIFF image pixel data with individual pixels aligned to
word boundaries (i.e. 8 bits, 16 bits, or 32 bits), you could use code like
the following:

```C++
#include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>
#include <functional>

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
  if (argc < 2) { return 1; }
  TiffCraft::TiffExporterAny tiffExporter;
  TiffCraft::load(argv[1], std::ref(tiffExporter));
  auto image = tiffExporter.takeImage();

  // your own image processing code

  return 0;
}
```

TiffExporterAny will decode and convert pixels to a flat-buffer (i.e.
 `std::vector<std::byte>`) with 1, 2, or 4 bytes per sample the source pixel
format. For example, an image with 2-bits per sample is exported as an 8-bit
image.

# Advanced usage

Users that prefer to decode and handle the image pixel data themselves, or need
to handle multiple frames per image, could write their own handler:

```C++
#include <tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp>
#include <iostream>

int main() {
  TiffCraft::load("image.tiff",
    [](const TiffCraft::TiffImage::Header& header,
        const TiffCraft::TiffImage::IFD& ifd,
        TiffCraft::TiffImage::ImageData imageData) {
      std::cout << "Loaded IFD with " << ifd.entries().size()
                << " entries." << std::endl;
      std::cout << "Image data size: " << imageData.size() << std::endl;

      // Add your own image processing code here

    });

  return 0;
}
```

# Features

TiffCraft supports the following features:

- Reading TIFF images
  - Read and display image metadata
  - Bilevel, grayscale, palette-color, and RGB images
    - Varying number of bits per sample
    - RGB images are supported only for 3-channel images (no extra samples)
- Compression is NOT supported yet.
- Writing TIFF images is NOT supported yet.

Advanced users could use TiffCraft for other configurations than those
enumerated above by writing their customizing any of the existing exporter
classes, or writing their own from scratch.

# CMake consumption

## FetchContent

TiffCraft is header-only and can be consumed directly from source with
CMake's `FetchContent` module:

```cmake
include(FetchContent)

FetchContent_Declare(
  TiffCraft
  SOURCE_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/third_party/tiffcraft
)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(TiffCraft)

target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE TiffCraft::TiffCraft)
```

When consumed this way, the `TIFFCRAFT_BUILD_ALL` option defaults to `OFF`,
so the library's tests, apps, and examples are not built.

## find_package

To consume a CMake-installed TiffCraft package:

```sh
cmake --install /path/to/tiffcraft/build/gcc-linux-release --prefix /path/to/install
```

```cmake
find_package(TiffCraft REQUIRED)

target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE TiffCraft::TiffCraft)
```

The installed package provides the `TiffCraft::TiffCraft` namespaced target and
the public headers under `include/tiffcraft`.

# Feedback

Feedback is welcomed! Please don't hesitate to reach out by opening a
[GitHub issue](https://github.com/danielm5/tiffcraft/issues/new/choose)
if you have suggestions, feature requests, or bug reports.

Please let me know if you find this project useful!

#!/usr/bin/env node
/* eslint-disable no-console */

const { run } = require('../src/cli');
const { stripDebugFlag } = require('../src/lib/debug-flags');
const {
  relaunchWithProxyEnvIfNeeded,
  applyUndiciProxyIfNeeded,
  readPersistedProxyConfig,
} = require('../src/lib/proxy-env');

const { argv, debug } = stripDebugFlag(process.argv.slice(2));
if (debug) process.env.TOKENTRACKER_DEBUG = '1';

const persistedProxy = readPersistedProxyConfig();
const relaunch = relaunchWithProxyEnvIfNeeded({
  argv,
  originalArgv: process.argv.slice(1),
  proxyConfig: persistedProxy,
});
if (relaunch) {
  if (typeof relaunch.status === 'number') process.exit(relaunch.status);
  if (relaunch.error) {
    console.error(relaunch.error?.stack || String(relaunch.error));
    process.exit(1);
  }
  process.exit(0);
}

// NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY only works on Node 22.21+/24.5+. For older runtimes
// (including community users on stale Node, and the embedded Node shipped
// with older macOS app builds), set an undici ProxyAgent so fetch() actually
// honors HTTPS_PROXY. Safe to run on modern Node too — explicit dispatcher
// takes precedence over the env-var-driven default.
const applyResult = applyUndiciProxyIfNeeded({ proxyConfig: persistedProxy });
if (applyResult && applyResult.unprotected === true) {
  console.error('[proxy] Manual proxy could not be applied and outbound traffic could not be blocked; aborting.');
  console.error('[proxy] 手动代理无法生效且无法阻断出站流量，已中止。');
  process.exit(1);
}

run(argv).catch((err) => {
  console.error(err?.stack || String(err));
  if (debug) {
    if (typeof err?.status === 'number') {
      console.error(`Status: ${err.status}`);
    }
    if (typeof err?.code === 'string' && err.code.trim()) {
      console.error(`Code: ${err.code.trim()}`);
    }
    const original = err?.originalMessage;
    if (original && original !== err?.message) {
      console.error(`Original error: ${original}`);
    }
    if (typeof err?.nextActions === 'string' && err.nextActions.trim()) {
      console.error(`Next actions: ${err.nextActions.trim()}`);
    }
  }
  process.exitCode = 1;
});

#!/usr/bin/env node
/* eslint-disable no-console */

const { run } = require('../src/cli');
const { stripDebugFlag } = require('../src/lib/debug-flags');
const {
  relaunchWithProxyEnvIfNeeded,
  applyUndiciProxyIfNeeded,
  readPersistedProxyConfig,
} = require('../src/lib/proxy-env');

const { argv, debug } = stripDebugFlag(process.argv.slice(2));
if (debug) process.env.TOKENTRACKER_DEBUG = '1';

const persistedProxy = readPersistedProxyConfig();
const relaunch = relaunchWithProxyEnvIfNeeded({
  argv,
  originalArgv: process.argv.slice(1),
  proxyConfig: persistedProxy,
});
if (relaunch) {
  if (typeof relaunch.status === 'number') process.exit(relaunch.status);
  if (relaunch.error) {
    console.error(relaunch.error?.stack || String(relaunch.error));
    process.exit(1);
  }
  process.exit(0);
}

// NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY only works on Node 22.21+/24.5+. For older runtimes
// (including community users on stale Node, and the embedded Node shipped
// with older macOS app builds), set an undici ProxyAgent so fetch() actually
// honors HTTPS_PROXY. Safe to run on modern Node too — explicit dispatcher
// takes precedence over the env-var-driven default.
const applyResult = applyUndiciProxyIfNeeded({ proxyConfig: persistedProxy });
if (applyResult && applyResult.unprotected === true) {
  console.error('[proxy] Manual proxy could not be applied and outbound traffic could not be blocked; aborting.');
  console.error('[proxy] 手动代理无法生效且无法阻断出站流量，已中止。');
  process.exit(1);
}

run(argv).catch((err) => {
  console.error(err?.stack || String(err));
  if (debug) {
    if (typeof err?.status === 'number') {
      console.error(`Status: ${err.status}`);
    }
    if (typeof err?.code === 'string' && err.code.trim()) {
      console.error(`Code: ${err.code.trim()}`);
    }
    const original = err?.originalMessage;
    if (original && original !== err?.message) {
      console.error(`Original error: ${original}`);
    }
    if (typeof err?.nextActions === 'string' && err.nextActions.trim()) {
      console.error(`Next actions: ${err.nextActions.trim()}`);
    }
  }
  process.exitCode = 1;
});

DESCRIPTION

USAGE
  opencode <subcommand> [flags] [<directory>]

ARGUMENTS
  directory string    Directory to start OpenCode in (optional)

FLAGS
  --standalone            Run with a private server instead of the background service
  --server string         Connect to a server URL instead of the background service

SUBCOMMANDS
  upgrade, update    Upgrade OpenCode to the latest or a specific version
  uninstall          Uninstall OpenCode, keeping session data, configuration, and state
  acp                Start an Agent Client Protocol server
  api                Make a request to the running server
  debug              Debugging and troubleshooting tools
  auth               manage integrations and credentials
  mcp                Manage MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers
  plugin             Manage plugins
  models             List all available models
  stats              Show shareable usage statistics
  mini               Start the minimal interactive interface
  run                Run OpenCode with a message
  session            Manage sessions
  service            Manage the background server
  reload             Reload configuration
  pair               Print one-time links to connect a browser or app
  serve              Start the v2 API and web server

- phase: "active", status: "expired"

- can_read_cloud: true

- trial_available: true

Upload error: HTTP 429: {"ok":false,"code":"cloud_sync_throttled","status":429,
"membership":{"phase":"active","status":"expired","has_gift":false,...,
"machine_limit":1,"can_read_cloud":true,"can_upload_cloud":false,
"read_only_until":"2026-12-09T05:52:14.603712+00:00", ...}}
```

So: your cron and the opencode plugin are both set up correctly and both paths have been trying to upload — they've just been getting throttled/refused by the cloud backend since ~3:00 PM yesterday. The local queue (~8 KB) is intact and will upload as soon as the cloud-side access is restored.

The actionable item is on the cloud account side: the device/membership needs to be resolved (renewed/handled through the paid multi-device policy) before uploads can resume.

First, thank you for building TokenTracker. I've used it since early on, across several machines, and I also helped with scan roots ([\#657](https://github.com/xiufengsun/TokenTracker/issues/657) / [\#725](https://github.com/xiufengsun/TokenTracker/pull/725)). I'm genuinely happy for you to make money from Cloud. Hosting costs money, and USD 4\.99/month is fair.

What I'd like to raise is how the change reached existing users:

- **No notice reached me.** I never got an email. Neither the macOS app, the menu bar nor the CLI ever showed a notification. I only found out when my devices started failing: `HTTP 409 cloud_machine_limit` on Nov 9, then `HTTP 429 cloud_sync_throttled`. The only place the transition date appeared was Settings → Cloud, which most people never open. Discussion [\#868](https://github.com/xiufengsun/TokenTracker/discussions/868) asks the same question and is still unanswered.

- **It's a big cut, not a small one.** Before, the free tier synced every few minutes from any number of machines. Now it's one device and one upload a day. For a tool whose value is seeing usage across machines, that's a large functional change. From a user's point of view, "it just broke" rather than "the plan changed".

Suggestions, offered as a supporter:

1. **Email every registered account** before a change like this, and again a few days before the transition ends.

2. **Show an in-app notice or banner,** plus a clear CLI warning, during the transition period, not just a line in Settings.

3. **Consider a discount or coupon for early users** who've been registered since before Cloud launched. It would turn a frustrating surprise into goodwill.

4. **Answer [\#868](https://github.com/xiufengsun/TokenTracker/discussions/868),** so others in the same situation know their history is safe.

Thanks again for the project. I'd just like the next change to land more smoothly for the people who've been with it from the start.

content.text:
That issue confirms exactly what's happening on your machine. It's the same reported problem, not a local config issue.

## This is a known cloud-side change, not your setup

The issue (opened Nov 10 by another affected user) documents precisely what you're seeing:

- TokenTracker cut free cloud sync to **one device and one upload per day**, without email notice or in-app warning.
- Affected users' devices started failing with `HTTP 409 cloud_machine_limit` (on Nov 9) then `HTTP 429 cloud_sync_throttled`.
- The old free tier synced every few minutes from any number of machines; now it's one device, one upload a day. The discussion linked in that issue (#868) asks the same "is my history safe" question and is still unanswered.

## How this maps to your machine

Your `tokentracker status` output matches the issue's description exactly:

```
Last upload: 2026-11-15T00:38:26.731Z
Next upload after: 2026-11-16T00:00:00.628Z
Last upload error: ... HTTP 429 cloud_sync_throttled ...
membership: { status: "expired", machine_limit: 1, can_upload_cloud: false, read_only_until: 2026-12-09 }
```

So your cron and OpenCode plugin are fine and have been trying — the cloud backend is actively rejecting the uploads because of this policy change (membership expired, one-device limit, read-only until Dec 9). Your ~8 KB local queue is intact and will upload once the cloud side lets it through.

## Bottom line

There is nothing to fix on this machine — the "problem" is the upstream TokenTracker cloud policy change that this GitHub issue is complaining about. To get uploads resuming you'd need to address it on the cloud side (e.g. activate the paid plan / resolve the device limit on your TokenTracker account). Since you clearly weren't notified and you're a long-time user, this issue is exactly the place to chime in — it plus the unanswered #868 discussion are where the maintainer is being pressed on it.
